title: Eventual commutativity of a finite interval of chain squares
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, F : I → CRing, i₀∈I, A = colimit F [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and P,Q cochain complexes of F(i₀)-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Fix i≥i₀ and a graded family vⁿ : Pᵢⁿ → Qᵢⁿ, where Pᵢ,Qᵢ denote extension from F(i₀) to F(i). Fix integers a,b. Assume that for every a≤n≤b the two composites vⁿ followed by d_Q and d_P followed by vⁿ⁺¹ become equal after extension from F(i) to A. Then there are j≥i and a graded family wⁿ : Pⱼⁿ → Qⱼⁿ such that the chain squares commute at j for a≤n≤b, and in every integer degree the extensions of wⁿ and vⁿ to A agree after the canonical scalar-extension comparisons [def-pc-complex-scalar-extension-hom]. No support bound, no map descent, and no equations outside [a,b] are asserted.

source.place: Tag 09RE, affine case (1), via Algebra Tag 05N7

proof.text: For each integer n in [a,b], form the two composites vⁿ d_Q and d_P vⁿ⁺¹ from Pᵢⁿ to Qᵢⁿ⁺¹. Extension of scalars preserves finite presentations, so both modules are finitely presented over F(i). Functoriality identifies the assumption with equality of the scalar extensions of these composites. Apply the equality clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] to obtain a later index where this equality holds. For a preorder the finite-presentation matrix proof uses only finitely many generator values, target relation witnesses, the filtered-ring elementwise criterion [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], and directed upper bounds. Equivalently transport through the mutual-comparability quotient equivalence before applying the partial-order theorem.

Choose j above i and every one of these finitely many indices. Extend every vⁿ to j, including degrees not in the interval, and conjugate by the canonical associativity comparisons to obtain wⁿ. Naturality with respect to both differentials identifies its square with the scalar extension of the corresponding square at i, which is equal at j. Associativity coherence identifies its further extension to A with that of vⁿ in every degree. For an empty interval take j=i and use identity-extension comparisons.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09RE affine case (1) and Algebra Tag 05N7; explicit graded-map and finite-square specialization by N4

lean.statement:
theorem eventually_commuting_finite_chain_squares
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ)
    (hP : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) (P.X n))
    (hQ : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) (Q.X n))
    (i : Set.Ici i₀)
    (v : ∀ n : ℤ,
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj (P.X n) ⟶
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj (Q.X n))
    (a b : ℤ)
    (hcomm : ∀ n : ℤ, a ≤ n → n ≤ b →
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map (v n) ≫
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map
          ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).map
            (Q.d n (n + 1))) =
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map
          ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).map
            (P.d n (n + 1))) ≫
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map (v (n + 1))) :
    let e (t : Set.Ici i₀) (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ) :=
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun r ↦
        ((ModuleCat.extendScalars r).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C)
        (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.w F (homOfLE t.property)).symm)) ≪≫
      (NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex
        (ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp (F.map (homOfLE t.property)).hom
          (colimit.ι F t.val).hom) (.up ℤ)).app C
    ∃ (j : Set.Ici i₀), i.val ≤ j.val ∧
      ∃ (w : ∀ n : ℤ,
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom).obj (P.X n) ⟶
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom).obj (Q.X n)),
        (∀ n : ℤ, a ≤ n → n ≤ b →
          w n ≫ (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom).map
            (Q.d n (n + 1)) =
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom).map
            (P.d n (n + 1)) ≫ w (n + 1)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, (e j P).hom.f n ≫
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F j.val).hom).map (w n) ≫
            (e j Q).inv.f n =
          (e i P).hom.f n ≫
            (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map (v n) ≫
              (e i Q).inv.f n)
